definition: How well a surface radiates compared with a black body: the power it emits from each square metre divided by $\sigma T^{4}$, the black-body value at the same temperature. It has no unit and lies between 0 and 1.

The fraction of the radiation falling on a surface or planet that is scattered back rather than absorbed: total scattered power divided by total incident power. It has no unit and lies between 0 and 1.

The intensity of the Sun's radiation at the top of Earth's atmosphere, on a surface at right angles to the rays, at the mean Earth–Sun distance; the data booklet gives $S = 1.36 \times 10^{3}\ \text{W m}^{-2}$.
